Shared contact/character damage, flash destruction and subtype BCD scores apply. The projectile falls toward terrain/player height, pauses ten updates, then moves horizontally until bounds or terrain.

Type five has two subtypes, selecting shape, colour and health. Clear its animation index and set the one-update guard, then return to the actor scan.

Restore subtype colour unless a surviving hit retains its flash nibble. Contact and character damage consume the subtype health counter. Subtype zero destruction allocates up to two subtype-one offspring with opposite curve phases; subtype-one has a one-update destruction guard. Ordinary subtype-zero animation cycles forty-eight colours, while offspring animate four shapes and follow a fifty-entry vertical curve with signed horizontal speed.

Type six initializes shape $EF and health twenty in state fifteen. After ordinary contact/weapon damage or flash destruction, fill free actor slots with randomized effect particles and request 5000 points. The randomizer combines a CIA timer, indexed program bytes and a local accumulator. Particle states move by signed stored speeds and reflect those speeds when sampled terrain is solid; timeout or bounds changes them to the resident effect type.

Bounds and lifetime end the particle. Otherwise move by stored signed X/Y velocities, derive its screen pointer and reverse vertical or horizontal speed when the corresponding sampled terrain properties are nonzero.
Type seven clears wheel mode. While the player is on the ladder-like state $29, active-low joystick left/right moves player X one half-pixel; otherwise release this actor.

Type eight emits up to nine seven-pose explosion cycles at timer/code-byte-mixed positions. Pose advancement has a three-update divider. Each new cycle chooses a sound channel through a four-entry table; completion releases the actor.

A gate/player sequence uses four phases. A negative gate flag locks input, installs a five-sprite raster and saved player callbacks, then starts sounds. Move the five gate columns down until an exact coordinate, patch nine screen cells and one map cell, shake horizontal scroll, wait a second counter and animate player departure. The later drawing path compensates gate columns for camera motion and restores the raster when their exact exit coordinate is reached.
Add two to five column positions. At coordinate $2A copy nine selected character codes into both screens, change map cell $95A5, request sounds and advance the gate phase.
Advance the departing sprite's half-pixel X and twenty-four-entry Y curve until its bound. Draw five gate sprites using high-X masks and a second five-shape raster band; choose raster line $96.

Once departure finishes, compensate gate columns for valid camera directions and restore ordinary raster/clear gate control at the exact selected position. Otherwise draw the five gate columns and the departing sprite.
Set five sprite Y coordinates to $9D and select the next raster callback at $74A6.

Type fifteen waits for the camera's fine phases and player movement state, adjusting the player near the entry boundary. Then install a five-column, seven-band boss raster, callbacks and damage glyphs; initialize the sixteen-bit counter to $044F. Subsequent calls update entry movement, action sequencing, contact, character damage and a falling/expanding terrain attack. Destruction changes actor slots into local explosion controllers and requests 15000 points.

Restore pending bitmap rows before another exchange. Before death, reset the colour matrix when needed, update entry movement/shake, dispatch an action, test contact/damage and animate the terrain attack. During destruction, flash the body and continue the terrain effect. Always prepare the next visible body band.
Follow a twenty-three-entry vertical entry curve while moving all five body columns left four pixels. Once the sampled terrain is solid, end entry and start shake/sound state.
Normally use vertical fine phase four. While the shake counter is nonzero, decrement it and choose a timer-derived phase zero through seven.

At the end of an action, select the next of eighteen action/duration records, resolve one of four low/high function pointers and clear action animation indices. Jump through the patched action target.

Cycle four six-band poses on a five-update divider. Copy shape, bitmap-low/high and colour sequences into the live matrix. Selected poses near the player push player X left two half-pixels and request a sound when terrain permits.

Cycle six pose selections with per-pose delays, copying three columns of three body bands and their bitmap pointers. At pose index three request the falling terrain attack. Also copy seven damage-scan offsets from the pose table.

Advance six poses on a four-update divider, replacing four columns of two bands and their bitmap pointers. Update four damage-scan offsets; completion requests shake and sound before the dispatcher selects another action.
Decrement the current action duration and clear its active flag at zero.
Convert the first column origin to half-pixel X. If in bounds, test five offset rectangles against the player and invoke the resident damage handler on contact.

After entry ends, scan sixteen row offsets for two adjacent character cells at $C8 or above. Consume a hit by writing $FF. Rows zero through four subtract the resident damage amount from the sixteen-bit $044F initial counter; high-byte underflow starts destruction. Other scanned rows consume the character without reducing the counter.

Flash all thirty-five body colours during a thirty-count destruction interval. Then restore saved raster hooks, request the shared flash effect, turn all eleven actor slots into local explosion actors, restore terrain glyphs, start deferred bitmap restoration and request 15000 points.
Copy ninety-six bytes of ordinary glyph graphics into $C008-$C067 and restore terrain properties one through twelve to solid.
After entry, if no terrain attack is active, derive the screen pointer from body band two, start its local state and request a sound.

Restore saved background characters and colours below the weapon-character threshold, then advance a two-by-two falling patch. On terrain contact, transition to an expanding four-column effect, saving and restoring its background through an eleven-entry width schedule. Timers and flash state end it; alternate two glyph patterns during expansion.
Convert a selected body band Y and first-column half-pixel X into the resident screen-row pointer and character column.
Shared entry using the current screen-row pointer: convert the first column X and high-X bit into a half-pixel origin, subtract the playfield margin and return the character column in $C1.

When the end-of-frame flag permits and a restoration request exists, exchange six consecutive 128-byte slices between $B800 and $F880. Keep source/destination pointers across calls and clear the request after all six slices.

Find the first visible body band, update five hardware sprite Y coordinates and choose the next raster line. At fine-scroll collisions, immediately exchange adjacent bitmap rows for the preceding band.

Install five shapes in both screen directories, five shared column X coordinates/high-X mask and five band colours. If another band approaches, wait on its raster distance and update the five Y registers.

Install five shape pointers in the active screen and colours for the current band. Restore previously exchanged bitmap rows, advance the band, set five sprite Y positions and choose the next raster callback. At matching fine-scroll phases, exchange bitmap rows through $802F before returning to the IRQ exit.
